selected.title: His Best Friend Matched With Me on a Dating App
selected.hook: My boyfriend's best friend matched with me on a dating app while we were still together.
selected.voiceover:
My boyfriend's best friend matched with me on a dating app while we were still together.

I wasn't using the app. My roommate was showing me profiles on her phone when she suddenly stopped scrolling and handed it to me.

There he was.

My boyfriend's best friend. Same photos. Same city. Same job. And his bio said, "Recently single, looking for something real."

I thought maybe he'd made the profile months ago and forgotten about it.

Then I noticed the account had been active that day.

I called my boyfriend and asked if his friend had broken up with his girlfriend.

He said, "No, they're fine. Why?"

So I sent him the screenshot.

Five minutes later, his friend called me directly.

He claimed someone had stolen his pictures.

Except one of the photos on the profile had been taken at my birthday dinner three weeks earlier. I knew because I was the one who took it.

Then my boyfriend admitted something worse.

He already knew.

Apparently his friend had been using dating apps for months, and my boyfriend had promised not to tell his girlfriend because it "wasn't our business."

That's when the argument stopped being about his friend.

Because if my boyfriend can help his best friend hide cheating, what exactly does loyalty mean to him?

He says protecting a friend doesn't mean he'd ever do the same thing himself.

Would you believe that?

A random dating-app profile turned into a much bigger relationship problem when she realized her boyfriend's best friend wasn't actually single — and her boyfriend already knew. Is keeping a friend's cheating secret just loyalty, or does it reveal something about your own values?
